chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, who said:
One of our companions wrote along with me to Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), asking him about the major sins, how many they are and what they are.

So he (عليه السلام) wrote: The major sins are those for which Allah has promised the Fire; whoever avoids them, Allah expiates his evil deeds from him when he is a believer. And the seven destructive ones are: killing the unlawfully protected soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury, reverting to bedouin ways after migration, slandering chaste women, consuming the wealth of the orphan, and fleeing from the battle line.

key_terms.عُقُوقُ ٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ: disobedience and undutiful conduct toward one’s parents
key_terms.قَتْلُ ٱلنَّفْسِ ٱلْحَرَامِ: killing a soul whose life is sacred and unlawful to violate
key_terms.مَالِ ٱلْيَتِيمِ: the property of the orphan, which must not be wrongfully consumed
key_terms.ٱلنَّارَ: the Fire, the divine punishment promised for such sins
key_terms.ٱلْفِرَارُ مِنَ ٱلزَّحْفِ: fleeing from the battlefield during combat
key_terms.ٱلْكَبَائِرِ: the major sins, meaning grave acts threatened with the Fire

ai.seo_question: What are the major sins mentioned by Imam Abī al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) in al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the major sins as those acts for which Allah has threatened the Fire, and states that avoiding them is a cause for expiation of lesser sins for the believer. It then names seven especially grave sins involving unlawful killing, parental rights, financial corruption, moral slander, violation of orphan rights, and cowardice in battle.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Mahboub who said,
‘One of our companions wrote along with me, to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the major sins, how many they are and what they are.

So heasws wrote: ‘The major sins one should avoid are what Allahazwj has Promised the Fire upon to expiate his sins from him, when he was a Momin; and the seven Obligating (such) are – killing a self unlawfully, and disloyalty to the parents, and consuming the usury, and the adoption of Pre-Islamic practices after the emigration, and slandering the married woman, and consuming the wealth of the orphans, and fleeing from the battle march’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Mahbub who has said the following:
“Once certain individuals of our people and I wrote to abu al- Hassan (a.s.) asking what and how many were the major sins.

He wrote back to us about major sins, ‘Whoever avoids the act for which Allah has decided to send one in the fire, his evil deeds are expiated, if he is of the believers. The seven acts that subject one to punishment are to commit murder, a disregard of kindness to parents, collecting unlawful interest in trade, alienating oneself from religion after accepting it, accusing married women of committing indecent acts, consuming the properties of orphans and running away from the enemy during an offensive in battle.’”
